examples.provenanceDetail: Authored for this thesis project (msc-4, Trong-Nghia Be) as a dedicated performance stress test -- classic k-coloring constraint satisfaction (one of Karp's 21 NP-complete problems), with no prior graph-coloring encoding anywhere in this plugin's history or this repository. The 40-Region/67-edge graph is generated using the 'flat graph' methodology of Culberson's flatNN-MM DIMACS graph-coloring benchmarks (partition vertices into k candidate color classes, add edges only across classes) so it is provably 3-colorable by construction while hiding that partition from the solver.
examples.question: Can Kodkod find a proper 3-coloring of a graph deliberately constructed to be tight at its own chromatic number (3 colors: satisfiable in seconds; 2 colors: quickly UNSATISFIABLE), and does every adjacent Region pair in the found solution actually differ in color?
oracleCaveats: This scenario's SAT verdict is only valid at bitwidth >= 8 (matching manifest.bitwidth and the hard-coded bitwidth:=8 in validate.cmd/query.cmd). At bitwidth 4-6, PropertyConfigurationVisitor's bitwidth-sufficiency check only validates declared Integer literal/attribute values, not Kodkod's internal encoding overhead for this scenario's 40-object self-referential relation with nested forAll -- so it silently returns a spurious near-instant UNSATISFIABLE with no warning (see constraints-and-configuration/config.bitwidth-insufficient-false-negative). If the harness is ever run at a lower bitwidth without updating this recorded expectation, the oracle would flip to a genuine false negative. The current SAT verdict itself is independently corroborated (check -v re-evaluation, a separate mv ? forAll query, and a graph-theoretic constructive 3-colorability proof), so this is a documented fragility to guard against, not a live concern.

examples.provenanceDetail: use-core/src/main/resources/examples/Others/Redefines/redefines.use, part of this repo's own bundled USE examples -- the original four-class/two-association structure (A, B; C < A, D < B; association AB between A/B; association CD between C/D, whose ends explicitly `redefines` AB's) is preserved exactly. The original had no attributes/operations at all, so attributes and invariants were authored on top purely to give Kodkod a real bounded search space and let a query reach an attribute (tagD) that exists only on the narrower redefining subclass -- this plugin had zero association-end-redefinition coverage anywhere in its history before this example.

examples.provenanceDetail: Authored for this thesis project (msc-4, Trong-Nghia Be) as a dedicated SAT-solver performance stress test -- the classic N-Queens combinatorial puzzle, chosen because its search space grows combinatorially with N while the OCL model itself stays tiny (one no-attack invariant). Row/Col distinctness is enforced structurally via mandatory 1-1 associations rather than via an extra arithmetic invariant, after an early attribute-only encoding was found (and confirmed via a hand-built check -v counter-example) to spuriously return UNSATISFIABLE -- traced to Integer_min/Integer_max bounds that covered the row/col domain but not the derived diagonal sums, not a plugin bug.
examples.question: How does Kodkod/DefaultSAT4J solving time actually scale in the classic N-Queens puzzle from a small (N=8, 92 solutions) to a deliberately large (N=17) board, and does the found placement genuinely have no two queens attacking each other?

examples.provenanceDetail: use-core/src/main/resources/examples/Others/Subsets/twoSubsets.use, part of this repo's own bundled USE examples, ported verbatim (zero syntax changes: same classes A/B/C/D/E/F, same three associations ab/cd/ef, same union/subsets declarations and multiplicities). Subsets.properties and both .cmd scripts are authored for this thesis project, since this plugin had zero coverage anywhere in its history of association-end subsetting (`role ... subsets ...`) or the paired `union` derived-end feature.
examples.question: Does the containment `subsets` requires -- every link in a subsetting association (cd, ef) is also a link in the union association it subsets (ab) -- actually hold in a found solution, and via what mechanism, given the plugin's own Kodkod-side translator never reads `subsets` at all and never instantiates its own dedicated `UnionAssociation` class?

examples.provenanceDetail: use-core/src/main/resources/examples/Others/Sudoku/Sudoku.use, part of this repo's own bundled USE examples -- the original Board/Row/Column/Square/Field class structure and operations are preserved, but the original ships a full 9x9 board hand-built via an ASSL script (Sudoku.assl/CreateBoard.cmd), never solved through Kodkod. Scaled down to a 6x6 board (2x3 boxes) after actually trying the original 9x9 scale first and confirming it is intractable here rather than assuming so: killed after 6m18s of unresolved DefaultSAT4J search at 24 givens/bitwidth 12, again after 2m30s at 24 givens/bitwidth 8, and again after 2m30s at 0 givens/bitwidth 8 -- all three still actively searching (past the near-instant 'trivially unsatisfiable' bounds check) when killed. Two previously-undiscovered plugin bugs were found and worked around while building this: (1) MultiplicityTransformator crashes on any fixed two-or-more-digit association multiplicity like the original's own `Field[81]` (worked around with `Field[*]` plus exact properties-file bounds); (2) per-object attribute-value binding (`ObjectName_attr = value`) is unconditionally broken for every model (worked around by encoding the puzzle's givens as coordinate-conditioned OCL invariants instead of properties-file bindings). See Sudoku.use/Sudoku.properties headers for the full detail and exact timings.
examples.question: Can Kodkod/DefaultSAT4J actually solve a genuine (non-trivial) Sudoku puzzle -- a 6x6 board with 10 givens -- in the seconds-to-tens-of-seconds range, given that the original bundled 9x9 board turns out to be intractable here, and does the found solution really have all 6 digits, with no repeats, in every row, column, and 2x3 box?
